origins: Family patterns can feel carved in stone: the same arguments, the same favorites, the same silence about hard things. After years of hoping and trying, it is natural to conclude that nothing will ever be different. Disappointment can turn into resignation or into a quiet bitterness.
teaches: Jesus said, “With man this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.” God promises, “I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you.” In Scripture, God changed the hearts of people who seemed hopeless, as in the story of the prodigal son. Proverbs says, “The king’s heart is a waterway in the hand of the LORD; He directs it where He pleases.” At the same time, we are told, “If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone.” We cannot force change, but we can pray, do our part, and keep our own hearts from hardening.
self_statements: Nothing I do makes any difference.
They will never see the truth.
It is pointless to try again.
I have to accept it forever.
errors: Predicting that no change will ever occur.
Believing change is either total or impossible.
Focusing on what has not changed and missing small shifts.
Feeling hopeless and concluding it is hopeless.
questions: What exactly do I want my family to change?
Has anything shifted over the years, even a little?
What part of this is mine to change, such as my responses or expectations?
What can I do differently while I pray for them?
What does Scripture say about God’s power to change hearts?
How can I protect my own peace?
truth: I cannot make my family change, but I do not have to give up hope. God can change hearts, and I can change my own responses. I can pray, set healthy limits, and live well whether or not they change.
hw_truths: With God all things are possible.
God can give a new heart.
I do not have to carry their change.
log: Each week, write one thing you did differently in your own responses.
actions: Write the specific change you hope for.
Write what is yours to change and what is not.
Pray for each family member for a week.
Decide how you will respond next time without waiting for change.
prayer: Lord, with You all things are possible. I place my family in Your hands. Change what only You can change, and change me where I need it. Give me peace. Amen.
hw_questions: What do I want to change?
What small shifts have I seen?
How will I protect my peace?
name_example: Sarah can write: “With God all things are possible, even for my family.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “My family will never change.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
